We need to actually call tools. First get functional groups list.


<thought>We need to locate a retrosynthetic template that corresponds to a nucleophilic aromatic substitution (S_NAr) where a halide leaving group is replaced by an amine nucleophile. This forward reaction breaks a “halide” functional group and forms an “amine” functional group, creating a C–N bond and breaking a C–X (halogen) bond. By searching the template catalog with these criteria we can retrieve the appropriate template, then obtain its mapped reaction SMILES and its template_id. The final answer will be a JSON object containing the mapped_rxn and template_id.
We need to actually call search_template_catalog_by_criteria. Use functional_groups_broken ["halide"], functional_groups_formed ["amine"], bonds_formed maybe ["6-7"] but not needed. Provide molecule_smiles? We need target molecule SMILES. Not given. Could use the precursor? But template search uses forward reaction criteria, not molecule. It also requires molecule_smiles. We could provide the product SMILES, but we don't have it. Maybe we can infer product SMILES by adding a halide to the aromatic position where the amine is attached. The precursor SMILES includes the amine attached to aromatic ring. The product would have a halide (e.g., Cl) attached instead of the amine, and the amine would be separate. However we don't know exact position. Could we just search without molecule_smiles? The tool requires molecule_smiles. Maybe we can use the precursor SMILES as the molecule to search templates that could apply to it (i.e., forward reaction). But we need template that when applied retrosynthetically to product gives precursor. The product is unknown. However we can still search templates that match the precursor (i.e., the amine attached) as a product of SNAr? Might still work.

Let's try using the precursor SMILES as molecule_smiles and criteria broken halide, formed amine.
